AOT AARCH64→C + SM86→SPIR-V STATIC RECOMPILATION & WINDOWS CLFS .CNPF DEFENSIVE AUDIT
adriadam10/mkw-recomp (★1,101 · 489-Commit AOT Recompiler) + MSNightmare/SignDrop (★422 · CLFS .cnpf Audit)
🏎️ adriadam10/mkw-recomp (★1,101 · MIT · AArch64→C + NVN2→Vulkan + SM86→SPIR-V)
1. Static Recompilation (Zero CPU JIT / Zero GPU Emulation)
• Lifts ARMv8.1–8.3 AArch64 (LSE atomics, CAS, LDAPR) ahead-of-time to native x86-64 / Linux AArch64 C
• Replaces 1,289 nn::* SDK imports by name & 699 NVN2 functions (529 shared + 170 new) over Vulkan 1.3
2. 489-Commit Disciplined AI Agent Engineering & Frame Budget Breakdown
11,561 SM86 Shaders → Tested offline (SASS → GLSL → SPIR-V) before any GPU game run
660M Frame Trace → ~3ms game logic + ~19ms Vulkan submit record + ~10ms GPU (~32ms)
60 FPS @ 2160p → 16.7ms on RX 7900 XTX (Win) & RX 9070 XT (Linux RADV)
In-Run A/B Gate → Measures perf inside same run (eliminates 12ms inter-run noise)
3. Container Seccomp & Mesh-Shader Fallback Mechanics
• Task/mesh shaders fall back to compute shaders automatically when VK_EXT_mesh_shader is absent
• Linux Docker/Podman requires userfaultfd in seccomp to track dirty game memory pages without slowdown
• Zero copyrighted assets shipped; builds on user's machine from user-owned dump
Architectural Takeaway for AI Solution Architects:
489 reviewed Claude Code commits in 10 days succeeded because of harness engineering: offline verification
across all 11,561 shader programs, seconds-long frame-capture backend replay without launching the game,
and within-run A/B timing to defeat 12ms run-to-run variance.
🛡️ MSNightmare/SignDrop (★422 · MIT · Windows CLFS .cnpf Mitigation Paradox)
1. When a Security Mitigation Introduces a New Attack Surface
• Oct 2025 CLFS authentication mitigation adds .cnpf HMAC files (90-day learning Mode=1 → enforcement Mode=0)
• In CclfsContainer::Create, opening a .blf log also opens associated AddLogContainer paths & signs empty containers
2. Privileged Coercion & DACL Inheritance Chain (Defensive Breakdown)
1. Standard User Setup → Creates .blf + associated empty container with user-controlled DACL
2. Privileged Coercion → Triggers ServerMpUpdateEngineSignature + Object Manager symlink
3. SYSTEM .cnpf Write → clfs.sys creates missing .cnpf as SYSTEM but copies original user DACL!
4. EDR Self-Defense Gap → File creation originates from AV's own process, bypassing driver filter
3. Enterprise Blue-Team Detection & Why You Must NOT Blindly Disable CLFS Auth
• Registry check: HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\CLFS\Authentication\Mode (0/1 exposed; 2/3 not)
• Catch-22: Disabling CLFS authentication re-exposes kernel memory corruption vulnerabilities in .blf parsing!
• Defensive priority: Monitor non-system .blf/.cnpf creation + Object Manager symlink joins + ServerMp* RPCs
Architectural Takeaway for AI Solution Architects:
Never assume `OBJ_FORCE_ACCESS_CHECK` at initial setup protects lazy side-effect file creation when
a different privileged caller opens the handle later and inherits the untrusted file's DACL.
Keep CLFS mitigation active while adding kernel ETW/Sysmon detection on .cnpf creation in protected dirs.
